content.thinking:
I'm planning the whole scene as one careful write: a roadside shrine prop group with lanterns, offerings, and a torii gate, styled in Genshin's cel-shaded aesthetic with gold filigree and glowing elements. I'm leaning toward an Inazuma theme—vermilion torii, electro-purple glow, gold trim, and scattered sakura petals, built from simple objects without needing joints.

A single root joint handles the whole structure, with everything else attaching to it by proximity. I'm laying out the scene in meters: a stone platform base, torii gate facing forward, a small hokora shrine on steps, paired stone lanterns flanking a path, glowing paper lanterns hung from the torii, an offering table with sake and rice, a saisen box, guardian fox statues, and a sakura branch, plus stone slabs, grass tufts, and shide paper strips on the shimenawa rope to round out the detail.

Now I'm sketching the helper functions I'll need -- lathe, extrude, sweep, cards, glow, and paint utilities -- and settling on a limited cel-shaded palette (vermillion, dark vermillion, black, gold, mottled stone, grained wood) built from reusable paint instances to keep the atlas small.

I'm also deciding on moss and lantern glow colors, picking amber and purple for the lantern crystals, then moving on to shape the torii pillars as tapered cylinders.

Still writing torii structure...

Still working out beam proportions...

For the central plaque between beams, I'm considering a small vertical box with a gold frame holding decorative text, though font rendering reliability is uncertain so I may just draw simple geometric glyphs instead.

I'm also planning the pillar caps and base rings in gold and black, plus a sagging shimenawa rope strung between the pillars with hanging shide paper zigzags and gold tassels at the ends, and I'm starting to think about adding paired chochin lanterns hanging from the nuki beam.

Now I'm designing the lantern geometry itself: a cord dropping from the beam to an ellipsoid lathe-shaped paper body, with thin dark torus rings as ribs, black lathe caps top and bottom, and a tassel hanging below, plus a small decal plane with the circular emblem placed just in front of the curved surface.

I'll go with b.decal applied to the lantern part, wrapping it in glow() since decal returns its own Part that needs glow applied separately. Now I'm sketching the shrine structure, starting with the stone plinth and cobble base dimensions before building up the steps.

Thinking through scale: the ground disc needs to be around radius 1.9-2.2 to accommodate the torii's kasagi width of roughly 2.9m, with the shrine foundation placed at the rear center around z=-0.55.

Now I'm working out the shrine foundation dimensions and a small entrance step in front of it, calculating box positions and heights so the step sits flush against the foundation edge.

Next I'm building the wooden shrine body itself: a floor deck, four vermilion corner pillars, and back/side wall panels. For the front, I'm designing two slightly-open door panels with gold lattice detailing, revealing a glowing purple crystal on a pedestal inside as the altar centerpiece.

Working out the mirrored hinge geometry for the right door...

For the gold lattice doors, I'm planning to render them as thin decal planes with a lattice texture positioned on the front face of each box, offset slightly outward and rotated to match the door's yaw, rather than texturing the whole box.

Now shifting to the roof design, I'm considering a hip-roof pyramid shape built using lathe geometry with 4 radial segments to get a square footprint, with a curved concave outline profile to create upturned eaves.

Still working out the roof curve coordinates...

Checking roof width against shrine width, that's fine proportionally. Now I'm thinking about tile coloring for the lathe roof, leaning toward a dark purple Inazuma-style palette, and working out a paint function that draws tile ridge lines based on distance from center in the slope plane.

I'll use chebyshev distance to create concentric square tile rows parallel to the eaves, then add perpendicular column lines by picking whichever axis dominates (x or z) to get the along-edge coordinate for cross-tile seams. Wrapping this in cel() with the paint function should give a nice stylized tile texture, and then I'll top the roof with a gold finial ornament made from a ball and spike shape.

Now I'm adding small gold cone tips at the four ridge corners, hanging gold bells with cords at each eave corner, a glowing purple octahedron crystal on a gold altar stand inside, and a suzu-style bell with red-white rope hanging from a beam at the shrine's front entrance.

I'm also placing a wooden saisen offering box with a slatted grate top in front of the shrine, deciding to hang the rope bell from the front roof eave center down to around y=0.5 instead of adding a separate gantry structure.

Still placing shrine elements...

Now I'm designing the stone lanterns as a stoneLantern function—stacking a hex-lathed base, post, platform, a glowing amber fire chamber with corner posts, a curved hex roof, and a finial gem on top, scaled to roughly 1.2 units tall.

I'm now adding a mossy stone shader using noise-based painting so patches of moss appear on upward-facing surfaces near the base, giving the lanterns a weathered look.

For the scene composition, I'm planning an offerings area beside the path steps—a low wooden tray holding sakura mochi, sake bottles tied with purple ribbon, a rice bowl, oranges, an incense burner, and a small sake barrel to add ritual detail to the shrine setting.

Now I'm adding an ema plaque rack near the torii with two posts and a beam, hanging five wooden wish plaques with simple svg drawings on cords — building them as thin extruded house-shaped outlines with wood material plus a decal plane for the artwork.

I'm also laying a stone path of rotated slabs leading from the torii to the shrine, and planning a sakura tree at the back-left with a curved trunk sweep and a canopy made from clustered flat-shaded blossom spheres, plus scattered petal cards on the ground.

Now I'm sizing the canopy spheres and positioning them around the trunk top, adding falling petals in flight, grass tuft cards around the disc rim and near the stones, and adjusting the overall disc radius to fit the tree and path comfortably.

For the torii, I'm placing it at the edge of the disc and budgeting part count to stay manageable. I'm detailing the pillars with gold bands, a black base collar, a daiwa ring, layered kasagi with gold end caps, shimaki, nuki, and a gakuzuka plaque, all painted vermilion with subtle wood grain variation and weathering that darkens the lower pillar sections.

Setting up gold paint as a flat color for the glow elements, then starting to write the actual builder code with a larger paint atlas size to accommodate the sizable painted surface area.

Defining the root joint and box/cylinder helper functions that wrap the geometry creation, noting that parts default to the nearest joint when no bone is specified.

I'm deciding when to use flat versus smooth normals — flat shading gives crisp faceted edges for gems or low-poly spheres, while smooth normals suit rounded cel-shaded forms like Genshin's style, so I'll expose this as an option in the helper. Now I'm planning the SVG textures needed, starting with a lantern emblem decal.

Writing SVG decal code...

Still working out the zigzag shide path...

Then I'll move on to designing the ema plaque drawings, three small decal variants in a 40x32 frame.

For the petal and grass elements, I'm sketching a sakura flower, a crescent-and-star motif, and a lightning bolt as separate decal options, then adding a simple pink petal shape and a layered green grass tuft with shaded blades for extra texture.

Next I'm thinking about the barrel decorations: a decal for the lid emblem, a simple label band with a red circle rather than text, and rope-wrapped bands modeled as torus rings on a straw-colored lathe barrel. I'm skipping any actual text in the decals and moving on to defining the cobblestone ground texture with varied gray-purple tones.

I'm then layering in mossy and grassy patches around the rim using radial distance checks warped with noise so the transition isn't a perfect circle, and sketching out a disc shape as a lathe profile with a few points to give it a beveled edge.

Now I'm placing stone path slabs leading toward the torii, sinking them slightly into the ground with small rotations and spacing them out in steps along the z-axis.

Checking placement so the fox pedestals, their grounded discs, and the lanterns don't overlap with the foundation steps, adjusting x and z offsets for each element until the spacing clears.

Checking tree and table distances to the rack, both look fine. Now I'm sketching the sakura tree's scale and trunk curve, positioning the canopy near the shrine roof so it overlaps slightly but stays clear of the lower structure, and working out the trunk's curve points.

Adding bark texture and canopy blobs...

Scattering fallen petals around the tree base and path using a circular distribution function, then adding airborne petals floating near the shrine at varying heights with random lean angles, keeping clear of the "nothing hangs above floor" rule. I'm also planning glow elements—lantern cores, shrine crystal, and tiny purple-glowing firefly motes floating around the shrine for ambiance.

I'm now positioning a glowing electro seal sigil as a flat ground disc near the torii, working out its radius and placement alongside the stone slabs so it sits centered beneath the torii without overlapping the offering box.

Working out the z-coordinates more precisely: foundation spans -1.25 to -0.25, the step sits at -0.25 to -0.03, and the saisen box lands at 0.02 to 0.38. I'm placing the bell rope near the front doors, which open outward around z=-0.4 to -0.2, so the rope hangs just in front of that.

Checking the door geometry — the left door hinge at x=0.46 swings forward to leave a gap clear from x=-0.31 to 0.31, so the rope at x=0 stays clear of the doors and the saisen box without overlapping.

Now I'm positioning the sigil at z=0.95 with a 0.45 radius, spanning roughly 0.5 to 1.4, and placing the torii pillars further out at z=1.05, x=±0.85 so they don't collide with it. I'm still working out exact placement for the stone slabs around z=1.7-1.95.

I'm checking spacing for the foxes, lanterns, barrels, and table against the shrine roof and tree — the table at x=-1.2, z=-0.6 clears the roof edge, and the tree trunk at (-1.55,-1.2) sits close to but doesn't overlap the table's footprint. Verifying the tree canopy clears above the table and that the trunk base stays just inside the 2.1-radius ground disc.

The trunk base radius pushes slightly past the disc edge, so I'm shifting the trunk to (-1.4,-1.1) and adjusting the canopy center to keep clearance, while confirming the canopy still overlaps the shrine's back roof reasonably since the roof height caps below the canopy's lowest point.

Setting up imports for the Three.js scene builder, frame, RNG, path interpolation, toon shading kit, glow effect, paint/texture utilities, and SVG texture helper, making sure every imported name gets used somewhere in the code to avoid unused-import errors.

Now I'm defining the build function with metadata for the wayside lantern shrine model, then setting up the builder with a root joint and a seeded RNG, and working out the color palette using gradient and cel-shading paints for parts like the kasagi, checking how the vertical gradient blends based on each part's y-position.

Writing palette definitions...

Writing ground paint function...

Adding grass tufts beyond a radius threshold, then setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and balls to simplify part creation.

Now I'm adding a torus helper that lies horizontal by default, rotating it about the X axis, and noting that caller-supplied rotation options take priority over this default orientation. I'm starting to sketch out how to build the torii gates themselves.

I need to figure out the kasagi curve geometry, letting pillars reach up to about 2.62-2.66 so they're hidden under the sloped beam, which dips lowest near the center (around y=2.69 at x=0) and lifts higher toward the ends (up to y=2.82).

Now I'm working out the base collar and gold band details for the pillar bottoms, defining their cylinder dimensions and torus placement.

Still placing pillar hardware details — the nuki crossbeam penetrating the pillars with protruding wedges (kusabi), plus a gold daiwa ring higher up at y=2.3.

Now I'm adding the kasagi roof-beam structure on top: a thicker black shimaki beam above a lower reddish section beam, shaping their cross-sections and considering gold end caps and trim at the beam tips.

For the gold end caps, I'm computing the slope at the kasagi's curved ends so the caps tilt to match the beam's rise, rotating each cap box about the z-axis by roughly ±10° depending on which end it's on. Then I move to building the nuki beam as a frustum box spanning across the pillars.

Adding frame and plaque geometry...

Now I'm working out the shimenawa rope between the pillars, using a sagging curve of points near y=2.0 that dips in the middle and rises toward each pillar, positioning it just in front of the pillar surface and below the nuki beam, with the ends wrapping around the pillars like tied rings.

I'm coloring the straw twist with an alternating pattern between two tan shades to simulate the woven texture, and planning the hanging shide paper strips as small card frames placed at intervals along the rope's curve.

For the rope ends, I'm adding small gold tassel shapes made from spikes and balls to give a decorative finish.

Now I'm sketching the hanging chochin lanterns from the nuki beams—placing them symmetrically at x=±0.45 with cords dropping down, dark caps, and a lathe-profile lantern body built from an outline of points to get that rounded paper-lantern silhouette.

I'm also adding thin decorative rib rings around the lantern body using small torus shapes, calculating their radii at different heights to match the lantern's curve, colored in a flat red.

Then I'm positioning a dark bottom cap cylinder and a downward-pointing gold tassel spike, plus an emblem decal placed on the lantern's surface.

Now I'm sketching out the shrine's foundation and decorative rim using box primitives with defined stone materials and z/y offsets, setting up variables to keep the structure consistent.

Still working out step dimensions...

Now I'm planning pillars as thin rods spanning the hall interior height, and setting up the back wall box with a cream plaster color.

Then I'm adding the front and side wall sections, horizontal roof beams and a lower rail in vermillion, and building out the altar interior with a pedestal and a floating crystal octahedron above it.

Now I'm adding a tilted gold ring around the crystal with small glowing motes, then placing dark red doors with lattice detailing at the shrine's front opening, hinged near the sides.

Working out the door panel angles and pivot positions so each door swings outward symmetrically from its hinge point...

Working out the door handle placement, positioning a small gold ball near the free edge opposite the hinge, computing the hinge offset relative to the door's local coordinate center based on the rotation angle.

Writing rotation helper and hinge/ring details...

Adding roof finial details with gold spikes and rings, plus small corner cones angled outward for decorative accents...

Now I'm working out hanging bells at the roof corners — small gold cones with clappers suspended by thin cords from the eaves, positioning them against the roof's inner edge height.

I'm checking the roof shell's thickness and corner beam alignment, confirming the eave edge roughly matches the beam top height, then thinking about adding thin gold fascia strips along the four eave sides to trim the upturned edges.

Since the facets are planar between ring vertices rather than curved, the actual mid-side height differs slightly from the simple radial interpolation—roughly 1.16 at half-width .74, 1.15 at .566, and 1.27 at .35, which is close enough for the approximation I'm using.

Now I'm placing a fascia box along the roof edge at y=1.13 with small depth, positioning it near half-width .745 so it sits at the roof's front edge, spanning the full 1.5 length with thin 0.03 thickness. I'm also confirming flat shading applies below 12-sided lathe segments, then adding the shimenawa rope and hanging shide decorations across the shrine's front beam, sagging between the two front posts with a separate bell rope in the center.

I'm reconsidering the rope placement since it conflicts with the open doors and beam position, deciding to skip the front shimenawa and instead focus on a gold suzu bell hanging inside the eave, with a twisting cord path leading down to a tassel.

Now I'm shaping the bell details—a dark slit opening and a top ring—then moving on to the saisen offering box, building its four corner posts and slatted-top body with proportions roughly 0.8 wide and 0.4 deep.

Adding trim pieces for the rim edges, filling the dark gap between slats, and placing a few flat gold coin cylinders on top.

Now I'm designing the stone lantern function, building it as a stack of lathe-generated hexagonal pieces—base, body, cap—using small polygon outlines to create the flared stone shapes at each height level.

Working out the node ball position on the post, then shaping the hexagonal platform and fire chamber dimensions for the lantern...

Still writing dimensions...

Still shaping the roof lathe profile...

I'm adding the finial on top with a stone ball and spike shape, keeping the scale factor simple at 1 for both mirrored lanterns, and planning to add moss texture to the base and hex sections via the stone paint material.

For the hexagonal lathe, I'm using 6 segments with default vertex orientation. I'm considering adding small hanging paper lanterns (chochin) on the sakura tree branches — two small glowing spheres with caps and cords for a nice touch. I'm also planning mirrored kitsune (fox) statues on pedestal boxes positioned symmetrically along the x-axis.

Now I'm defining the stone fox statues: setting up a mottled whitish stone texture for the fox color, then shaping the sitting fox body as a leaning ellipsoid with separate haunch geometry positioned slightly above the base.

I'm continuing to lay out proportions for front legs, paws, and head, checking that the head height and body scale stay consistent with the pedestal so the fox looks proportionally correct when sitting.

Now I'm positioning the snout as a forward-tilted cone with a dark nose ball, then adding outward-tilted ear cones with potential inner-ear accents, followed by placing small eye details.

Then I'm setting dark eye slits near the head front, a red neck bib torus with a gold bell, and a tail built from a curved catmull sweep with tapering radii from base to tip.

For the fox's traditional jewel, I'll give the s=1 fox a glowing purple jewel sphere held near its paw, and the s=-1 fox a gold scroll instead, skipping whiskers and ink mouth details for simplicity. Now I'm starting the offerings table on the left side with a flat rectangular tabletop.

Building the table legs and cloth runner, then shaping a sake bottle using a lathe profile with a white ceramic finish and a subtle blue decal band.

Still shaping the cup polygon profile, then adding a rice mound using a flattened hemisphere geometry colored off-white sitting atop the bowl.

For the fruit offering, I'm placing a lacquered red tray on legs with three orange spheres and small green leaf cones on top, and separately building a dango skewer with pink, white, and green mochi balls stacked along a thin rod.

I'm also adding an incense burner with a bronze bowl, a few leaning incense sticks, and tiny glowing orange ember tips at their ends, skipping the smoke effect for simplicity. I'm settling the table dimensions as a 0.7x0.45 top centered around (-1.2, 0.4, -0.6), so I can position all these small items accurately within that bounding area.

Now I'm placing straw barrels near the shrine, stacking one atop another with a smaller one beside them, using a lathe profile to shape each barrel with a bulging mid-section and flat top and bottom. I'm adding rope-band torus shapes near the top and bottom of each barrel, a flat wooden lid disc, and a decal label on the front combining a white rectangle with a red emblem and blue stripe to sell the "goods barrel" look.

Skipping the ladle, I'm placing a ema rack with two support posts at x=-1.5 and checking they fit within the disc radius at that z-position.

Now I'm figuring out the roof geometry for the structure: a ridge beam along x at the top, with two angled boards sloping down on either side to form a gable, using rotations about the x-axis to create the slant.

Then I'm placing the ema plaques hanging from the beam, spacing a few across the front within the post width.

For the plaque hanging detail, I'm using thin cord rods from the beam to the plaque corners, plus a second lower row from the rail, giving six plaques total at different heights with varied drawings. Then I'm defining a house-shaped pentagon outline for each ema plaque and extruding it along the x-axis to give it thickness.

I'm extruding the ema outline with wood-colored paint, facing the front since the shrine faces +Z, and adding a small bevel for a rounded edge. For the decal drawings, I'm placing textured planes slightly offset in front of each plaque surface, using white as the base color so the drawing's own colors show through properly.

Now I'm scattering foot stones at the post bases and adding grass tufts near lantern bases and corners, using randomized positions and sizes with cross-plane cards for coverage. I'm also adding a handful of glowing firefly motes and considering mossy path slabs between the stones for texture.

Then I'm designing a purple glowing ground sigil as an SVG with concentric circles, an eight-pointed star, and rune ticks, mapping it onto a glowing plane oriented upward on the ground to cast a mystical emblem beneath the structure.

With part placement mostly settled around 350 pieces, I'm now sketching a small lantern emblem SVG with a circular outline for additional decoration.

Now I'm designing the plaque and lattice icons, setting proper viewBox scales and stroke widths for the torii sigil with gold accents and corner dots, then moving to the door lattice grid dimensions.

For the EMA drawings I'm sketching simple symbolic icons—sakura blossoms with pink petals and a yellow center, a crescent-and-star motif, and a purple bolt—choosing colors that stand out clearly against the wooden plaque background.

Drawing grass blade shapes...

Now I'm placing pink petal clusters around the tree blob, working out positions and radii for several overlapping spheres to form the blossom canopy.

I'm also roughing out the trunk as a tapered set of points with shrinking radii, then adding thin branch rods connecting trunk points outward to support the blossom clusters.

Checking that the trunk base and lowest canopy blobs stay above the table surface, then setting up a surface scatter to place blossom cards on the canopy blobs, filtered to upward-facing normals.

Now I'm positioning hanging paper lanterns off the branch tips, with cords dropping down and glowing lantern balls near each tip, while checking that the lantern positions don't collide with the table underneath.

I'm also scattering floating glowing motes near the shrine and generating petal cards on the ground around the tree, placing them randomly within a disc around the tree's base while filtering out ones that fall outside the radius.

Now I'm making sure the frame import is wired correctly for the petal cards, and double-checking type strictness for the color helpers—reconciling `ColorInput` and `Fill` types so the `Paint` import works cleanly without unused-locals errors.

Starting the build function...

Working out the radius parameter typing...

I should instead use an explicit tuple-returning function to avoid typing ambiguity, and confirm the section box orientation matches the lantern's up/binormal axes correctly. Now I'm checking each lathe outline shape—hex lantern foot and platform points—to make sure none of them self-intersect.

Checking the roof, chochin, and shrine roof outlines next, verifying the point ordering sweeps consistently from axis outward to rim and back without crossing, and that sharp corners stay intentional creases rather than smoothing errors.

For the lathe geometry, I'm confirming that with four segments and a 45° spin, the resulting vertices land on the diagonals rather than the axes, which is what I want for the silhouette shape.

Now I'm sketching outline coordinates for several objects — a disc, barrel, bottle, and cup — checking each profile's point sequence to make sure the resulting lathe stays monotonic in height and doesn't self-intersect, which would create invalid geometry.

Setting the tori with low radial segments for a faceted look, and working out the table height: legs centered at .24 with height .28, top box centered at .4, so items rest at y=.42.

Placing the sake bottles with lathe geometry and a purple neck ribbon torus, then positioning two red lacquer cups with gold accents nearby, and a rice bowl lathe shape rounding out the table setting.

Now I'm adding the dango skewer with a wooden holder and stacked colored balls on a stick, then positioning a fruit tray and oranges on the table, and starting on an incense burner placement.

Adding incense sticks with glowing ember tips...

I'm also double-checking item x-positions stay within the table bounds and mentally tallying flat color strings since I'm using cel-shading for most objects to keep the palette count low.

Now I'm confirming imports are all used—noise for stone texture, INK for eyes—and planning a helper function to rotate door offsets before writing the ground lathe geometry.

Writing ground lathe shape...

Now I'm adding a ring of edge stones around the rim, using boxes placed at angular positions with rotation computed so each stone's long axis aligns tangent to the circle.

Writing the full build script now, setting up imports, color palette with vermilion gradients, and the torii pillar loop with rope tassels...

Checking lantern placement against the rope geometry to make sure the cords cross the shimenawa naturally without clipping, then moving on to positioning the plaque planes with their rotations.

Writing stone lantern function...

Still placing roof pieces and finial...

Now I'm sketching the fox pedestal placement, positioning the stone base box and top slab at specific heights so the body sits correctly at yb=.34.

Working out the body geometry... haunch, legs, paws, head, snout cone with a tiny ink nose at the tip.

Still placing ears and eyes...

Still shaping the bib, bell, and tail geometry...

For side details I'm thinking about chest fur and markings, but simplifying by skipping stripes and keeping the fox coloring plain. I'm also placing a glowing jewel prop and a small rolled scroll as a mirrored accessory for the opposite side.

Now I'm planning the broader scene coding: a cards helper for billboarded sprites using frame vectors, scattered grass tufts around the shrine area with randomized angle and radius, and clusters near lantern bases, fox pedestals, and ema posts.

Then I'm adding floating petals in the air with randomized positions, leaning angles, and spin, plus a handful of glowing motes as small spheres, before double-checking all imports are actually used.

Now I'm laying out the ema plaque rack: posts, rods, and beams positioned with vermillion-colored boxes to form the wooden frame structure.

Still placing plaques and cords...

Still working out the plaque rotation and plane offsets...

Checking that everything stays above y=0 — disc base, lathe, torii, tree canopy all line up correctly. Now writing a rotation helper function for positioning the door lattice panels at their angled offsets.

Still writing door geometry...

Let me also consider adding nobori flags near the torii as extra decorative dressing to give it a more festival-like feel.

Positioning the pole with a crossbar and hanging banner geometry, adding a gold finial and stone base, then setting up the banner planes with front/back texturing...

Glow should apply fine to lathe and textured parts since they aren't using the "paint" material name, and decal targeting works on the lantern lathe part. Time to write out the full file now.
